en: Therīgāthā 5.3 Pañcakanipāta Sīhātherīgāthā The Verses of the Elder Nun Sīhā I am a lioness, O lion; I have entered the lion’s lair. Having slain the elephant with tusks like plowshafts, I dwell in peace. My mind is well-liberated; I am free from fear, without dread. I am a nun, O King; I am not one who belongs to you. “Through improper attention,
tormented by sensual lust,
I was previously agitated.”
Lacking mastery over the mind,
she is overwhelmed by defilements and follows after the perception of beauty.
I found no composure of mind,
following the power of a lustful heart;
emaciated, pale, and discolored, I was.
For seven years I wandered;
afflicted by great suffering, I found no happiness by day or by night.
Then, taking a rope,
I entered the middle of the forest:
"Better for me to hang myself here."
And whatever is base, one should practice again.
Having made a firm noose and having bound it to the branch of a tree;
“I cast a noose around her neck,
and then my mind was liberated.
… Thus spoke the Elder Nun Sīhā.
